Up to four invisible strips sit at the screen edges: two on the left and two on the right, each covering the 10-40 percent or 60-90 percent band of the screen height. From a strip you swipe in one of three directions - up, down, or inward - and every swipe runs the action assigned to it: a screenshot, the camera, device control (flashlight, volume, brightness), opening an app, and more. Which zones are on, whether their guides are visible, and the action per direction are all set in \"Configure gestures\". Requires the \"Display over other apps\" permission.

Lets FastMediaSorter take screenshots with an edge gesture and save them, with no per-shot dialog. This covers screenshots only - screen video recording is separate and asks Android for permission at the start of every recording.

To take screenshots with the edge gesture, turn on the FastMediaSorter accessibility service:

1. Tap Open settings, then enable FastMediaSorter in the accessibility list.
2. If it shows Controlled by restricted setting or App was denied access: open this app in App info, tap the menu (3 dots), choose Allow restricted settings, confirm, then go back and enable it.

If you cannot enable it, tap Old method to use a version that asks for permission on every shot.
